title: NSW SSD/SSI Application-Class Accuracy Instantiation and Temporal Allocation Qualification Closeout

scientific_finding.summary: The NSW SSD/SSI aquifer-interference framework is a real decision context in which groundwater drawdown predictions, model accuracy, uncertainty, monitoring and mitigation matter. The available application-class authorities do not prescribe a transferable numerical prediction-accuracy allowance and do not allocate a numerical share of such an allowance to coupling temporal error.
scientific_finding.H_app_finding: The NSW Aquifer Interference Policy explicitly compares near-threshold exceedance with the accuracy of an otherwise robust model, which validates the decision-margin concept, but does not provide a numerical application-class prediction-accuracy requirement. The IESC uncertainty guidance independently states that acceptable mismatch and acceptable risk are project/QoI specific.
scientific_finding.A_temporal_finding: NSW modelling guidance requires temporal discretisation to be appropriate to objectives and stress changes and requires uncertainty analysis, but supplies no numerical fraction or amount of prediction-error budget reserved for coupling temporal error.
scientific_finding.consequence: The canonical F-GC09/F-GC10 contract seam must remain uninstantiated for AC03 until a concrete project, regulator-approved modelling plan, condition of approval or equivalent governed application contract supplies both numerical policy inputs with provenance.

rejected_substitutions: physical Level-1 drawdown threshold used as H_app
calibration residual, RMS or normalised RMS target used as H_app
measurement or instrument accuracy used as H_app without a decision rule
solver closure tolerance used as H_app
generic stress-period/time-step guidance used as A_temporal
F-GC07 coupling error magnitude or convergence rate used to choose H_app or A_temporal

architecture_invariants.9: PASS: no day/month/year coupling assumption introduced
architecture_invariants.10: PASS: flexible coupling windows remain possible; no fixed window selected
architecture_invariants.11: PASS: coupling policy remains explicit runtime/coupler functionality
architecture_invariants.12: PASS: application head-error policy remains separate from the hard head/flux interface contract
architecture_invariants.13: PASS: mass conservation remains absolute and is not allocated into the error budget
architecture_invariants.14: PASS: GC07 numerical sensitivities/indicators remain first-class evidence but cannot choose application policy
architecture_invariants.15: PASS: no extra production SWAP runs introduced
architecture_invariants.23: PASS: application accuracy policy remains separate from physics and solver policy
architecture_invariants.26: PASS: provenance and fail-closed diagnostics are explicit
architecture_invariants.28: PASS: application-class composition remains runtime/coupler responsibility
architecture_invariants.29: PASS: no silent NSW, calendar, file-format or MODFLOW dependency added to the kernel

hard_nonclaims: No numeric H_app for NSW SSD/SSI is qualified.
No numeric coupling head-error budget is qualified.
No statement is made that all NSW projects share one prediction accuracy.
No regulatory impact threshold is relabelled as numerical model tolerance.
No production SWAP-MODFLOW coupling configuration is admitted.

downstream.entry_condition: A concrete project-specific or regulator-approved source must explicitly provide a numerical groundwater-head/drawdown prediction-accuracy requirement or decision margin, plus an independently governed numerical allocation to coupling temporal error. If only one is supplied, the other remains fail-closed.

exact_head_requirement: The commit introducing this closeout must pass the F-GC11 NSW application-class accuracy qualification workflow.
